solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tiger seen unusually in area of Tanzania

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters fall in an unexpected order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A safari visitor spots a tiger somewhere in Tanzania, which would be a surprise since tigers live in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is quietly absurd: there are no wild tigers in Africa, which is why the sighting is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the vast plain and national park in northern Tanzania famous for its wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Reportedly leaves auctions

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the word is said

parts.note: to leave port is to sail, so leaves can be sails, which is pronounced the same as the plural of sale

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone is quitting the auction houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a noun (foliage) but is the verb, as a ship sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctions are sales in which goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Get back sappers' mining rights

parts.note: sappers are army engineers, the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE
a claim is the plot a miner has the right to work

explanation.surface: Army engineers recover their right to dig.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in Britain they belong to the Royal Engineers, RE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover possession of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Terrible man in North America hosts Queen and this band

indicators.note: in places one thing inside the other, here the man inside the continent's letters

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: a host takes a guest inside, so the man takes the monarch within him

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An awful man in America has Queen and another rock band on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock group and is not part of the definition; the clue's own band is the one being defined, so 'this band' points back to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was the American grunge rock group fronted by Kurt Cobain, so it is a band like Queen.

clue.text: Result of opening on-line first

indicators.note: first tells us which piece leads, so the online letter is placed at the front

parts.note: E as in e-mail, electronic, stands for online
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: The outcome of launching something on the internet first.
explanation.walkthrough: E for electronic is the crossword shorthand for anything online, as in e-mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome, as in 'in the event', so it is a synonym of result.

clue.text: Horrible Republican obscures liberal growth

indicators.note: to obscure is to cover up, so the new letter is put over the old one and hides it

parts.note: inclement weather is horrible weather
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A nasty Republican hides a liberal's progress, a political complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L in INCLEMENT for R to get INCREMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase or addition, the amount by which something grows.

clue.text: Difficult material you reportedly disposed of for the setter

indicators.note: one thing thrown out and another put in its place, a swap

parts.note: stuff is cloth or fabric

indicators.note: reported speech, so the pronoun stands for the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U is said like the word you
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: Hard-wearing fabric you got rid of on the compiler's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from STUFF and put I in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff means hard or demanding, as in a stiff test, a synonym of difficult.

clue.text: Outrage of backsliding boys put in prison …

indicators.note: the boys are placed around the jail as if wrapping it
sliding back in a down entry means reading the word from the bottom up

parts.note: lads are boys
can is slang for jail

explanation.surface: Public fury that reoffending young men have been jailed, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the reversed boys go around the prison; 'put in' is read loosely as the prison put in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public outrage caused by shocking conduct.

clue.text: … meanwhile I am supporting abrupt inmate

indicators.note: abrupt means cut off suddenly, so the word loses its last letter
in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: to intern is to imprison, and an internee is an inmate
I am contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: in the meantime I am backing a curt prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: An intern is strictly a person held in confinement; cut short it is INTER, with IM below.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim as an adverb means in the meantime, matching meanwhile.

clue.text: Fictional account of river area around Kent

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the South East is the region round Kent
hood is short for neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A made-up tale about the region near a Kentish river.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east of England; the Fal is a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue statement, a story that is not fact.

clue.text: The stars briefly meet bird in Swiss city

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the stars are what supposedly govern our fortune
the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: Celebrities meet a girlfriend in a Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The stars' suggests celebrities or astronomy, but here it means fate, as in a horoscope.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a city in central Switzerland on the lake of the same name.

clue.text: Personal effect of gossip changing hands

indicators.note: switching from one hand to the other means right becomes left

parts.note: chatter is idle talk

explanation.surface: A personal item from a rumour of a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands are right (R) and left (L): swap the final R of CHATTER for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is a movable item of personal property, which the law calls a personal effect.

clue.text: Mastic maybe transported around Alabama

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: transported means sent away
the standard abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: Tree resin shipped round the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: Alabama's old postal abbreviation is the three-letter form used here, not the two-letter AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin-based paste used to seal joints, an example of a sealant, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Support what a East End knacker may do!

parts.words: what a East End knacker may do!
parts.note: surface: a London horse slaughterer's job

parts.words: what a East End knacker may do!
parts.note: setter's reading: a knacker kills an old horse, ending it, and a Cockney drops the h of horse, as the clue's 'a East' hints

explanation.surface: A slaughterman in London's East End giving his backing to something.
explanation.walkthrough: A knacker buys worn-out horses for slaughter; in Cockney, the dialect of London's East End, the h is dropped, so 'end horse' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or back publicly, so it is a synonym of support.

clue.text: Tower in main place rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form

parts.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tower in the town square has been reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a bell tower, usually free-standing, as in Italian cities.

clue.text: Observe judge squashed by bigwig

indicators.note: in a down entry, being squashed by something means lying underneath it

parts.note: a celebrity, an important person
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Watching a judge being flattened by a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to mark it, which is what celebrate means.

clue.text: Bizarrely maintain Earth is lifeless

indicators.note: bizarrely means strangely, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An odd claim that the planet is dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means not alive, without the spirit of a living thing.

clue.text: A follower gets into car in an uncertain state

indicators.note: getting into a vehicle puts one inside it

parts.note: short for limousine
B follows A in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A hanger-on climbs into a car without knowing where it is going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A follower' reads as someone's fan, but it is the letter after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of being in between, waiting for a decision, hence uncertain.

clue.text: Three animals seen in Castle Ashby

indicators.note: seen in means visible within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A trio of creatures spotted at an English stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Castle Ashby is a stately home in Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is an old hunting term for a set of three hounds, hares or other game.

clue.text: Need self-denial to give up money

indicators.note: giving something up means letting go of it, so letters are removed

parts.note: abstinence is denying oneself pleasures
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone has to practise self-restraint and stop spending cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TIN out of the middle of ABSTINENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An absence of something is a lack or want of it, which is one sense of need.

clue.text: Lead attached to radio equipment for telephonist

parts.note: to head is to lead
a radio is a set, as in a wireless set

explanation.surface: A cable plugged into a radio for a switchboard operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like an electrical cable, but it is the verb meaning to be at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset combines earphones and microphone, the kit a telephone operator wears.

clue.text: What a prospective guardian may be next

definitions.text: What a prospective guardian may be
definitions.meaning: someone wanting to become a guardian is seeking a child in care, a ward

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'after ward': a would-be guardian is after (seeking) a ward, a young person under guardianship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at a later time, so it serves as an adverb for next, as in 'what happened next'.

clue.text: Make steady progress to incriminate man in court

parts.note: to rat on someone is to inform against them

indicators.note: in places the man inside the abbreviation for a court

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a man is a he

explanation.surface: A prosecutor working step by step to frame a man in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratchet is to move by small increments in one direction, like the toothed mechanism, so steady progress.

clue.text: Butcher married girlfriend?

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack apart, so the letters are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Did the butcher get married to his girlfriend?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' reads as the man in the story, but it is the verb that scrambles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A girlfriend may be someone's admirer, one who is fond of them; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Graduates' note includes section for some rice

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one letter sits inside the rest

parts.note: two graduates, a Bachelor and a Master of Arts
te or ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
s is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: University graduates' memo includes a part on what rice to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduates'' gives two degrees, BA and MA; with the note after them, S slips in between the two degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grained fragrant rice from South Asia, one kind of rice.

clue.text: The very best drug contains a hint of temazepam cut with a trace of methadone

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the drug wraps one letter
drugs are cut with other substances mixed in, so another letter goes inside

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug

indicators.note: a hint is just a small taste, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of this sedative

indicators.note: a trace is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this opioid

explanation.surface: A dealer's boast that the finest drug is laced with other narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate single letters are inserted at different points, the way a dealer bulks out a drug with other substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum describes the most favourable or best possible condition, so it matches the very best.

clue.text: Give a view on poetic description of tree?

parts.note: O is the poet's address, as in an ode beginning 'O ...'
a pine is a conifer

explanation.surface: A request to comment on how a poet would describe a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Poets address things with 'O', so a verse to a tree might start 'O pine'; the question mark flags this loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine on something is to state an opinion about it.

clue.text: Allow order to return in traveller's accommodation

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: let means allow
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Permission for an instruction to come back to a guest's lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, an exclusive British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel designed for motorists, a place for travellers to stay.

clue.text: Breakdown in amines seen before a medical condition

indicators.note: a breakdown splits something into pieces that can be put together anew

parts.note: taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on how certain compounds decompose before an illness appears.
explanation.walkthrough: Amines are organic compounds derived from ammonia, a deliberately technical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a medical condition.

clue.text: Be the recipient of hot lady's sex appeal

parts.note: hot, meaning fashionable, is in
her is the possessive for a woman
it is an old word for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Being on the receiving end of an attractive woman's allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' reads as temperature or attraction but means trendy, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property or traits passed down, so to be the recipient of them.

clue.text: Wield authority dismissing Penny

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: an expert is an authority on a subject
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Using power to fire a woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'authority' suggests power, but here it is a person who knows a subject well.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence or force is to wield it, to bring it to bear.

clue.text: Elite examination in this college

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective completing the phrase 'electoral college'

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A top-class test at a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this college' points to the electoral college, the body that formally chooses the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completed by the answer names a body of voters, so the adjective fits as a description of that college.
